title: rbac-v2: enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers in regulated environments require stronger guarantees that KMS usage and key material remain in-region and that all KMS key selection events are auditable. This change hardens RBAC v2 policy enforcement to ensure KMS region pinning is enforced for resources that opt into residency policies, and it wires additional audit logging hooks so we capture both policy decisions and the resolved KMS key metadata (key id, region, and policy source). Motivation: Reduce accidental cross-region key selection and make policy decisions observable for compliance reviews. Changes: 1) Policy evaluation: add explicit KMS residency check in the RBAC v2 evaluator; failure mode is now a deny unless the resource has an explicit "allow-cross-region-kms" exception label. 2) Audit logging: emit structured audit events for KMS resolution (kms.key_resolve) with fields: user, principal, requested_region, resolved_region, key_id, policy_id. Events are emitted to the existing audit log pipeline and an additional compliance topic for long-term retention. 3) CLI/Installer: add migration step to detect resources relying on implicit cross-region KMS behavior and surface recommended remediation. 4) Tests: unit, integration, and e2e (installer path) updates. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated on "rbac_v2_kms_pin_hardening". Default off for 48 hours after merge; enable in non-prod a day after, then staged rollout to production with monitoring. Checklist: - [x] Policy evaluator changes and unit tests - [x] Audit event schema and pipeline wiring - [x] Installer migration + discovery script - [x] Integration tests against mock KMS/residency store - [x] Documentation updates (RBAC v2 policy docs) - [x] Security review done (SEC) - [x] Rollout runbook added Testing: local unit tests + integration suite passed in CI; ran end-to-end installer flow in a staging cluster and validated audit events in the compliance topic. Backwards compatibility: default is opt-out (feature-flag off), migration provides recommendations before enforcement. If the feature is enabled and a resource fails the residency check it will be denied until remediated; we consider this a non-breaking behavioral tightening for customers who opt into the policy. Related: references ENG-9821 for evaluator perf improvements and SEC-1140 for audit retention requirements.
